notes: Batch W (pantoprazole, dexlansoprazole, domperidone, metoclopramide, ondansetron, itopride). All 445 quotes checked FOUND against fetched page text on 2026-10-17. | NO UK PRODUCT: dexlansoprazole and itopride - no emc results by ingredient or clinic trade name, no NICE results. The MHRA products search API (medicines.api.mhra.gov.uk/graphql) returned HTTP 503 on every attempt during this session, so MHRA products could NOT be checked for these two; re-check when the service is back. | DOMPERIDONE TABLETS: emc lists only two domperidone products (1 mg/mL oral suspension, 10 mg orodispersible tablet). No standard 10 mg tablet SmPC found on emc and MHRA products unavailable (503); the 10 mg orodispersible tablet SmPC is used for the clinic 10 mg tablet (content identical to the suspension SmPC apart from excipients and the antacid timing line, which appears only in the suspension SmPC). | MHRA domperidone: 2014 DSU restricted indication to nausea/vomiting, max 30 mg/day, usually max 1 week, new cardiac contraindications; its original child dose (0.25 mg/kg) is superseded by the Dec 2019 DSU (no longer licensed under 12 years or under 35 kg). July 2026 DSU adds phaeochromocytoma contraindication (present in both SmPCs used). | GROUP INFERENCE: domperidone 4.3 contraindicates QT-prolonging drugs. Metoclopramide and ondansetron are added to qt-prolonging from SPS (metoclopramide: mainly IV; oral ondansetron: low risk without risk factors), so domperidone + metoclopramide/ondansetron will show as contraindicated via the group rule although neither is named in the domperidone SmPC (dolasetron is). Integrator may wish to review. | CONFLICTS: metoclopramide breastfeeding - SmPC not recommended vs SPS use with caution short term; ondansetron breastfeeding - SmPC should not breastfeed vs SPS use with caution; ondansetron pregnancy - SmPC should not be used in first trimester vs BUMPS can be used for pregnancy sickness (MHRA: counsel and decide jointly); pantoprazole pregnancy - SmPC preferable to avoid vs BUMPS other PPIs can be used if advised. Rules use the stronger SmPC level and name the other source in action. | Domperidone severe renal impairment is defined only by serum creatinine > 0.6 mmol/L (no CrCl/eGFR), so it is a condition rule on severe-renal-impairment, not a numeric renal rule. Metoclopramide CrCl ≤15 and 15-60 rules both match at exactly 15 mL/min (source boundary overlaps). | Ondansetron MHRA IV dose restrictions (2013 DSU) are IV-only and not applied to the oral clinic product; only its oral-relevant reminders (avoid in congenital long QT) are cited. | BUMPS URL /leaflets-a-z/metoclopramide/ serves the general nausea and vomiting in pregnancy leaflet (covers metoclopramide, domperidone and ondansetron). No BUMPS domperidone leaflet exists (404). | emc-101124 (cabergoline SmPC) is used only to source the metoclopramide-cabergoline contraindication and metoclopramide dopamine-antagonist membership. | Not mine: sources/E.json and C.json define sps-macrolides-statins with different URLs (pre-existing conflict). | AUDIT 2026-10-17 (independent check, see audit/V-W.md): MHRA products search retried once (medicines.api.mhra.gov.uk/graphql still HTTP 503); emc search re-run for dexlansoprazole, itopride and both clinic trade names: no results, so both stay no-uk-product. emc search for domperidone still lists only the 1 mg/mL suspension and 10 mg orodispersible tablet. QT group check against SPS: domperidone, metoclopramide and ondansetron meet the QT policy (SPS lists all three; the ondansetron SmPC states dose-dependent QT prolongation). Other batches: SPS states sertraline has no effect on QTc at licensed doses, so by the QT policy sertraline should leave qt-prolonging (batch D); this currently makes the domperidone QT contraindication fire for sertraline.
